To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the palynological data from core LB1, San Gregorio Formation, Baja California, Mexico, provide evidence for a semiarid, neritic coastal marine environment during the late Oligocene.
the San Gregorio Fm. palynoflors were dominated by marine taxa (dinocysts, acitarchs, copepod and foraminiferal eggs), which were deposited in a nerititic marine environment.
San Gregorio palynofloral assemblages are composed mainly by marine palynomorph associations and, to a lesser extent, by terrestrial palynomorph associations.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the first detailed palynological study of the San Gregorio Fm. in Baja California Sur.

the San Gregorio Fm. was deposited in a semiaride coastal marine environment, where a palaeoaltitude gradient was present, with a temperate climate, which allowed the development of highland vegetation (e.g. Pinus forest and a cloud forest).
the palynomorph assembages of the SGF at LB1 are indicative of a coastal marine environment, with a palaeoaltitude ranging between 0 and 500 m, where the climate was semiarid, warm and humid.

the San Gregorio palynofloral assemblages were the product of an interaction of the following palaeoenvironmental parameters: 1) the local vegetation, 2) the palaeoaltitude and the palaeoaltitude of the study area, 3) the local hydrographic system, 4) the local climate, 5) the local marine environment, and 6) the palaeogeographic setting of the region.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the San Gregorio Fm. core LB1 was a semiarid neritic marine environment, with a temperate highland climate, where the vegetation was dominated by a cloud forest, a Pinus forest, and local semiarid plant communities, such as chaparal, tropical deciduos forest, coastal grasslands and coastal dunes.

The main takeaway from our work is that
the palynological assemblages of the San Gregorio Fm. at LB1 reflect the palaeoenvironmental conditions of the coastal marine setting in Baja California Sur during the late Oligocene.

the palynoflors recovered from the SGF at LB1 reflect the presence of two temperate communities: a highland Pinus forest and a cloud forest, and a palaeoecosystem that includes a semiarid vegetation along an altitudinal gradient, which includes a coastal dune.
